entries.answer:
Ez a három kérdés a Perplexity Computer minőségbiztosítási infrastruktúrájának, konszenzusmechanizmusának és böngészőautomatizálási rétegének belső architektúráját vizsgálja.



 82. Belső benchmarking és A/B tesztelési keretek

 Intézményi benchmarkalapú kiértékelés

A Perplexity legnyilvánosabban dokumentált belső kiértékelési kerete az intézményi benchmarkösszehasonlítás: az "Everything is Computer" blog 16 000 lekérdezésen mért, McKinsey, Harvard, MIT és BCG intézményi benchmarkokhoz viszonyított eredményekről számol be. Ez nem csupán marketing – egy 16 000 lekérdezéses vizsgálat strukturált kiértékelési infrastruktúrát feltételez, amelyen belül különböző orkesztrációs stratégiák összehasonlíthatók egymással. A HLE, Browsecomp és SimpleQA benchmarkokat a Perplexity AI értékelési módszertan leírása is azonosítja mint az LLM képességek mérésének fő szisztematikus módszereit.[1][2]

Az orkesztrációs stratégiák A/B tesztelése a termelési forgalom szintjén zajlik: az aicerts.ai Enterprise elemzés leírja, hogy "engineers monitor token budgets through credit consumption dashboards within the AI computer console". Ez a credit consumption dashboard nem csupán számlázási eszköz – hanem az orkesztrációs stratégia hatékonyságának proxymérőszáma. Ha egy alternatív routing stratégia ugyanolyan minőségű kimenetet produkál kevesebb tokenköltséggel, ez az A/B teszt döntő metrikai jele. A gend.co Model Council elemzés pontosan ezt az értékelési logikát fogalmazza meg: "treat models like components you evaluate, monitor, and swap — not magic boxes you hope behave" – és ehhez valid összehasonlítási infrastruktúra szükséges.[3][4]

 A workflow audit mint folyamatos A/B szignál

Az ability.ai elemzés leír egy különösen releváns belső benchmarking mintát: az orkesztrátor saját maga auditálja a workflow kimeneteit egy előre definiált minőségi kritériumrendszer alapján, és ezek az auditeredmények akkumulálódnak visszajelzési adatként. "By automating the audit layer, operations teams can instantly identify weaknesses and seamlessly pass those insights to another agent designed to execute the necessary fixes" – ez pontosan az a folyamatos, önirányított A/B loop, amellyel az orkesztrációs stratégia finomhangolódik production data alapján. A PARL tréning keretrendszer ezeket az akkumulált auditeredményeket megerősítő tanulási szignálként dolgozza fel, zárva a körforgást a production kiértékelés és az orkesztrátor javítása között.[5]



 83. Multiagent vita és konszenzus nézeteltérés esetén

 A Model Council mint formalizált deliberáció

A Model Council a Perplexity multiagent konszenzus mechanizmusának legelőrehaladottabb megvalósítása: egyetlen kérdést három modell – Claude Opus 4.6, GPT5.2 és Gemini 3.1 – párhuzamosan dolgoz fel, majd a rendszer az egyezéseket és nézeteltéréseket explicit összehasonlítással szintetizálja. A LinkedIn elemzés pontosan a nézeteltérést azonosítja mint a legértékesebb szignált: "transparency into WHERE models disagree – the most valuable signal". Ez azért kritikus, mert ha mindhárom modell megegyezik, az erős konfidenciaindikátor; ha kettő megegyezik de egy nem, az a kérdést tovább vizsgálandóvá teszi; ha mindhárom eltér, a rendszer eskalál emberi felülvizsgálathoz.[4][6]

A deliberatív döntési mechanizmus nem egyszerű szavazás: az eltérő vélemény tartalmát az orkesztrátor elemzi, és ha az ellenvetés érvényes logikai alapon áll – nem csupán stochasztikus varianciából ered –, az ellenvetést alkotó modell lekérdezési sorrendje megváltozik, és az eltérés okát célzott followup kérdéssel vizsgálja meg. Ez a "dissent analysis" megközelítés különbözteti meg a Model Councilt az egyszerű ensemble módszerektől: nem az átlag, hanem a legfontosabb információtartalmú eltérés irányítja a végső szintézist. Az Facebook kommentár szóhasználata – "like hosting a mini AI debate inside your browser" – pontosan ezt a deliberatív jelleget fejezi ki.[7][5][4]

 A nézeteltérés kezelésének három kimenetele

A nézeteltérési protokollnak három különböző kimenetele lehetséges az eltérés természetétől függően. Az első: faktuális eltérés – ha a modellek különböző tényállításokat hoznak, a rendszer forrásverifikációt indít, és a forrással alátámasztott állítás nyer. A második: stratégiai eltérés – ha a modellek különböző következő lépéseket javasolnak, az orkesztrátor a DAGban legkisebb visszafordítható utat választja, és opcionálisan humán döntést kér. A harmadik: értékelési eltérés – ha a modellek egy kimenet minőségéről nem értenek egyet, a ResultVerifier 80%os küszöbrule dönti el, hogy a kimenetet elfogadjáke vagy visszaküldik revizióra.[6][5]



 84. Böngészőautomatizálás réteg és megfigyelhetőség

 Az elkülönített felhő böngésző architektúrája

A böngészőautomatizálás az egyik legjobban dokumentált alrendszer a Perplexity Computer architektúrában, részben azért, mert a biztonsági kutatók reverseengineering vizsgálatai részletesen feltárták. A singhajit.com részletes elemzés rögzíti: a böngésző egy elkülönített felhő böngésző, teljesen szeparált a helyi rendszertől és az alügynöki sandboxtól – ez három izolációs réteget jelent: a helyi eszköz, az orkesztrátor, és a böngésző egymástól fizikailag szétválasztott futtatási kontextusokon futnak. A böngésző az alügynök toolhívásain keresztül kapja az utasításokat, és az elvégzett akciók eredményeit – screenshot, DOMkivonat, visszatérési értékek – strukturált payloadként adja vissza az alügynöknek, aki tovább adja az orkesztrátornak.[8]

Az implementáció valószínűleg Playwright vagy Puppeteer alapú böngészőautomatizálási libraryt alkalmaz, amelyet a Perplexity szandbox infrastruktúra köré wrapperelt. A megfigyelhetőség szempontjából kritikus korlátot ugyanaz az elemzés azonosítja: "in our experience, there is no rich live preview of what the browser agent is doing" – a felhasználó nem lát valós idejű képernyőképet a böngésző tevékenységéről, csupán a befejezett lépések szöveges összefoglalóját. Ez a "megfigyelhetőségi gap" a böngészőautomatizálási réteg egyik fő gyakorlati korlátozása.[8]

 A zerotrust egress proxy mint böngészőbiztonsági réteg

A böngészőautomatizálás biztonsági rétegének legfontosabb komponense a zerotrust egress proxy: minden egyes kimenő hálózati kérés – böngésző navigáció, API hívás, fájlletöltés – ezen a proxyn megy keresztül, amely verifikálja, hogy a kért erőforrás az engedélyezett desztinációk listáján szerepele. Ez megakadályozza, hogy egy rosszindulatú webhely által injektált prompt a böngészőügynököt belső erőforrásokhoz vagy más felhasználói adatokhoz irányítsa. A proxy a credential injekciót is kezeli: amikor a böngészőügynöknek authentikált munkamenetre van szüksége egy SaaS platformon, a raw API kulcs vagy OAuth token soha nem kerül be a böngészősandbox futtatási kontextusába – a proxy injektálja a szükséges hitelesítési fejléceket az alkalmazás szintjén, a sandbox felett.[9][10]

 Replit Agent Prompt



Build a complete, productionready, multimodel AI search and agent orchestration platform on Replit. The system consists of five layers: a React/TypeScript frontend, a Python FastAPI gateway layer, an Inkolanguage agent orchestration core, a Ziglanguage lowlevel performance runtime, and a multiprovider inference and tool backend. Every file must be complete, unabridged, and immediately runnable. No placeholder logic, no TODO comments, no stub implementations, no mock data, no simplified versions. Every integration must call real APIs with real credentials sourced from Replit Secrets.



 ENVIRONMENT SECRETS

Configure the following Replit Secrets before generating any code. Every secret must be read from os.environ or the equivalent in each language layer. Never hardcode credentials.

 LAYER 1 – FRONTEND (React + TypeScript + Vite)

Include dependencies: react@^18, react-dom@^18, typescript@^5, vite@^5, @vitejs/plugin-react, zustand@^4, @tanstack/react-query@^5, axios@^1, reactflow@^11 (for DAG visualization), tailwindcss@^3, @tailwindcss/typography, framer-motion@^11, lucide-react, react-markdown, remark-gfm, eventsource-parser, socket.io-client@^4.

 frontend/src/App.tsx

Implement a full singlepage application with a left sidebar (navigation: Search, Computer, Deep Research, Memory, Skills, Audit), a main content area that renders the active panel, and a right panel for agent activity timeline. The application must connect to the gateway via WebSocket on mount for realtime agent event streaming. Implement dark and light theme toggle with localStorage persistence. No authentication screens – the app is fully open on load.

 frontend/src/components/SearchBar.tsx

Implement a search input that submits queries to POST /api/search/query. Display a model selector dropdown listing all available models: azure:last-v3, azure:bibi-v3, glm-5, grok-4.1, tensormesh:auto, modal:auto, best (orchestrator choice). Implement streaming response rendering by consuming a ServerSent Events stream from GET /api/search/stream/:session_id. Display inline citations as superscript numbers linked to the CitationList component. Render thinking/reasoning steps as a collapsible "reasoning trace" section above the final answer.

 frontend/src/components/AnswerPanel.tsx

Render the full model response with: Markdown rendering including tables and code blocks with syntax highlighting, inline citation superscripts, a confidence badge (high/medium/low derived from source count), a "copy" button, a "regenerate" button that reroutes through a different model, and a source count summary line. Show the model name and token count used in a footer bar.

 frontend/src/components/CitationList.tsx

Render numbered citation cards. Each card contains: the source title, domain, publication date, a 2sentence excerpt, the relevance score from Exa, and a direct link. Group citations by domain. Show a "Webset" badge on citations retrieved via Exa websets.

 frontend/src/components/ModelCouncil.tsx

Render a threecolumn panel showing simultaneous responses from three models to the same query. Highlight where models agree (green border) and where they diverge (amber border). Show a "Synthesis" panel below the three columns containing the orchestrator's final integrated response. Add a "Dissent Analysis" section that explains why the models disagreed where they did, generated by the orchestrator.

 frontend/src/components/ComputerPanel.tsx

Implement the Computer workflow interface. At the top, a naturallanguage goal input. Below it, a realtime task graph (using ReactFlow) that renders the DAG as the orchestrator builds it, with nodes colored by status: gray (pending), blue (running), green (completed), red (failed). Below the graph, an AgentTimeline showing each subagent's start time, model used, duration, token count, and output summary. At the bottom, a spending cap display showing tokens consumed and a manual "pause workflow" button.

 frontend/src/components/TaskGraph.tsx

Use ReactFlow to render a directed acyclic graph. Nodes have: label (task name), model badge, status indicator, and clicktoexpand detail showing the full handoff payload and output. Edges show dependency direction. Autolayout using dagre. Animate running nodes with a pulsing border. Support zoom and pan.

 frontend/src/components/SandboxOutput.tsx

Show the Daytona sandbox execution output in real time. Implement a terminalstyle black panel with monospace green text for stdout and red for stderr. Show the exit code, execution duration, and files created. Add a "View Files" button that opens a file tree of the sandbox filesystem at the point of last execution.

 frontend/src/components/DeepResearchPanel.tsx

Implement a full Deep Research interface. Input field for the research question. Below it, a collapsible "Research Plan" tree that shows the current todo list with completed items checked off. A "Findings" panel that streams partial results as each subagent completes. A "Draft Report" panel that shows the incrementally built document. At the top right, a stats bar showing: search queries issued, total tokens consumed, sources cited, iterations completed, and elapsed time.

 frontend/src/components/SkillsEditor.tsx

Implement a skills management panel. List all saved skills with name, description, last used date, and run count. "New Skill" button opens a modal with: skill name field, description field, and a large textarea for the instruction set in natural language. "Test Skill" button runs the skill on a sample input and shows the output in a sandbox preview. Skills are saved to the gateway via POST /api/skills.

 frontend/src/components/ApprovalGate.tsx

Implement a modal that blocks workflow execution when the orchestrator raises a humanintheloop escalation. Show: the proposed action description, the action type (reversible/partiallyreversible/irreversible), the specific tool call parameters, a risk assessment, and two buttons: "Approve" and "Reject". Approvals must be submitted to POST /api/computer/approve/:action_id within 120 seconds or the action autorejects.

 frontend/src/components/AuditLog.tsx

Render a paginated, searchable audit log table with columns: timestamp, session ID, event type, model used, token count, action taken, and outcome. Support filtering by event type and date range. Export to CSV button.

 frontend/src/hooks/useComputer.ts

from daytona import Daytona, CreateSandboxParams
import os

class DaytonaService:
    def __init__(self):
        self.client = Daytona(api_key=os.environ["DAYTONA_API_KEY"], server_url=os.environ["DAYTONA_SERVER_URL"])

    async def create_and_run(self, code: str, language: str, files: dict = None) -> dict:
        params = CreateSandboxParams(language=language)
        sandbox = self.client.create(params)
        try:
            if files:
                for filename, content in files.items():
                    sandbox.fs.write(filename, content)
            result = sandbox.process.code_run(code)
            return {
                "output": result.result,
                "exit_code": result.exit_code,
                "stderr": getattr(result, "stderr", ""),
                "files_created": [f.name for f in sandbox.fs.list("/workspace")]
            }
        finally:
            sandbox.delete()

 LAYER 3 – INKO AGENT ORCHESTRATION CORE

The Inko agent core is a standalone HTTP server that listens on port 9000. It handles orchestration, model routing, subagent lifecycle, DAG execution, and humanintheloop escalation. All concurrency uses Inko's lightweight process model (one Inko process per subagent).

inko
import std.net.tcp (TcpServer, TcpClient)
import std.io (Read, Write)
import std.json (Json)
import orchestrator (Orchestrator)
import meta_router (MetaRouter)
import tool_registry (ToolRegistry)
import skill_engine (SkillEngine)
import checkpoint_store (CheckpointStore)
import audit_trail (AuditTrail)

class async Main {
  fn async main {
    let router = MetaRouter.new
    let tools = ToolRegistry.new
    let skills = SkillEngine.new
    let checkpoints = CheckpointStore.new
    let audit = AuditTrail.new
    let orchestrator = Orchestrator.new(router, tools, skills, checkpoints, audit)
    let server = TcpServer.new(ip: '0.0.0.0', port: 9000).get
    loop {
      match server.accept {
        case Ok(client) -> {
          let handler = RequestHandler.new(client, orchestrator)
          handler.handle
        }
        case Error(e) -> {}
      }
    }
  }
}

Implement the Orchestrator class with the following methods:

fn start_workflow(goal: String, skills: Array[String], spending_cap: Int, session_id: String) – Parse the goal into a DAG using plan_from_goal. Spawn one Inko process per DAG node that has no dependencies (fanout). Each process runs a SubAgent. Collect results via channels. When all dependencies for a downstream node are resolved, spawn its process. Continue until all nodes complete or the spending cap is hit. Write checkpoint to CheckpointStore after each node completion. Publish progress events to the gateway via HTTP POST to http://localhost:8000/api/internal/event.

fn plan_from_goal(goal: String, skills: Array[String]) -> Dag – Call the primary orchestrator model (Azure last v3) with a structured prompt that instructs it to output a JSON DAG with nodes having fields id, task_description, model_preference, tool_calls_allowed, reversibility, and depends_on: Array[String]. Parse the JSON response into a Dag struct.

fn handle_search(query: String, model: String, exa_results: String, session_id: String) – Select the model via MetaRouter.select. Construct the full prompt with Exa results injected as context. Stream tokens back to the gateway Dragonfly channel via HTTP.

fn pause_workflow(session_id: String) – Set a flag in the session state that all running subagent processes check on their next iteration.

fn resume_workflow(session_id: String) – Clear the pause flag. Reenqueue all pending DAG nodes.

 agent_core/src/sub_agent.inko

Implement SubAgent as an async class (Inko process). Constructor accepts task: DagNode, parent_plan_summary: String, shared_memory_context: String, tool_registry: ToolRegistry. The run method:

1. Constructs the full system prompt by injecting parent_plan_summary and shared_memory_context.
2. Calls the provider corresponding to the node's model_preference via the appropriate provider module.
3. Parses tool call requests from the model response and executes them via ToolRegistry.
4. If a tool call has reversibility == "irreversible", POST to http://localhost:8000/api/computer/request_approval with the action details and block until the approval decision arrives (poll Dragonfly key approval:{action_id} every 2 seconds, timeout 120 seconds, reject on timeout).
5. After tool execution, feed the observation back to the model for the next iteration.
6. Repeat until the model emits a terminal output marker.
7. Return the SubAgentResult struct containing: output, citations, tool_calls_made, tokens_used, status.

Implement "diminishing returns" detection: if three consecutive iterations produce outputs with cosine similarity > 0.97 (computed via a simple tokenoverlap Jaccard similarity), emit the current output as terminal.

Implement topological sort of the DAG using Kahn's algorithm. Implement the execution loop that maintains a ready_queue of nodes with all dependencies satisfied, a running_set of actively executing nodes, and a completed_map of node results. After each node completes, check which downstream nodes now have all dependencies satisfied and add them to ready_queue. Spawn a new Inko process for each node in ready_queue. Implement spending cap enforcement: after each node completion, sum all tokens_used values; if the total exceeds spending_cap, drain ready_queue without spawning and mark remaining nodes as skipped.

 LAYER 4 – ZIG LOWLEVEL RUNTIME

 runtime/src/main.zig

Implement a lightweight TCP server on port 9001 exposing three endpoints called from the Inko layer:

 /count_tokens – Accept a UTF8 string body, return exact token count using a BPE tokenizer implementation (GPT4 tokenizer vocabulary, hardcoded cl100k_base vocab table).
 /compact_context – Accept a JSON body { messages: [...], target_tokens: int }. Apply sliding window compaction: keep the system message intact, keep the last N messages that fit within target_tokens, and prepend a summary header line "[Compacted: {removed_count} messages removed]". Return the compacted messages array as JSON.
 /schedule_parallel – Accept a JSON array of task specs with estimated durations. Return a topological sort and parallelism schedule that minimizes critical path length using list scheduling.

 runtime/src/token_counter.zig

Implement BPE tokenization using the cl100k_base vocabulary. Load the vocabulary from an embedded byte array at compile time using @embedFile. Implement count(text: []const u8) usize that returns the exact token count. Implement truncate_to_tokens(text: []const u8, max_tokens: usize) []const u8 that returns the prefix of the text that fits within the token budget.

 runtime/src/context_compactor.zig

Implement the context compaction algorithm. Input: messages: []Message, target_tokens: usize. Strategy: (1) Always preserve the system message. (2) Always preserve the last 4 messages. (3) Extract key claims from the middle messages using a simple heuristic (sentences containing named entities, numbers, or decision keywords). (4) Format the extracted claims as a compact bulletpoint summary. (5) Return the system message + summary + last 4 messages.

 runtime/src/latency_tracker.zig

Implement a ringbufferbased latency tracker that records the last 1000 perprovider latency measurements. Expose p50(), p95(), p99() functions. The Inko metarouter queries this via /latency_stats to make routing decisions.

 LAYER 2 – INKO BACKEND (entire backend, port 8000)

The Inko backend is a single binary that serves all API routes, manages WebSocket connections, runs the agent orchestrator, communicates with all external APIs, and writes to all databases. It runs on a single TCP port 8000. All concurrency is handled with Inko's lightweight process model: each HTTP request spawns a shortlived process, each subagent spawns a dedicated process, and channels connect processes.

 backend/src/main.inko

inko
import std.env (Environment)
import std.net.tcp (TcpServer)
import router (Router)
import storage.dragonfly (DragonflyClient)
import storage.singlestore (SingleStoreClient)
import storage.supermemory (SuperMemoryClient)
import tools.exa (ExaClient)
import tools.daytona (DaytonaClient)
import orchestrator.orchestrator (Orchestrator)
import orchestrator.meta_router (MetaRouter)

class async Main {
  fn async main {
    let env = Environment.new
    let dragonfly = DragonflyClient.new(url: env.get('DRAGONFLY_URL').get)
    let singlestore = SingleStoreClient.new(
      host: env.get('SINGLESTORE_HOST').get,
      port: env.get('SINGLESTORE_PORT').or('3306').to_int.get,
      user: env.get('SINGLESTORE_USER').get,
      password: env.get('SINGLESTORE_PASSWORD').get,
      database: env.get('SINGLESTORE_DATABASE').get
    )
    singlestore.run_migrations
    let supermemory = SuperMemoryClient.new(api_key: env.get('SUPERMEMORY_API_KEY').get)
    let exa = ExaClient.new(api_key: env.get('EXA_API_KEY').get)
    let daytona = DaytonaClient.new(
      api_key: env.get('DAYTONA_API_KEY').get,
      server_url: env.get('DAYTONA_SERVER_URL').get
    )
    let meta_router = MetaRouter.new(env)
    let orchestrator = Orchestrator.new(meta_router, exa, daytona, dragonfly, singlestore, supermemory)
    let router = Router.new(orchestrator, dragonfly, singlestore, supermemory, exa, daytona)
    let server = TcpServer.new(ip: '0.0.0.0', port: 8000).get
    loop {
      match server.accept {
        case Ok(client) -> {
          let conn = Connection.new(client, router)
          conn.handle
        }
        case Error(_) -> {}
      }
    }
  }
}

fn start_workflow(goal: String, skills: Array[String], cap: Int, session_id: String) – Step 1: call plan_from_goal to get a Dag. Step 2: write the DAG to SingleStore and publish a dag_initialized event to WebSocket. Step 3: run DagExecutor.execute(dag, session_id, cap). Step 4: on completion, write final status to SingleStore and publish workflow_completed event.

fn plan_from_goal(goal: String, skills: Array[String]) -> Dag – Construct a system prompt that instructs the model to return a JSON object with a nodes array. Each node: { "id": string, "task_description": string, "model_preference": string, "tools_allowed": [string], "reversibility": "reversible"|"partial"|"irreversible", "depends_on": [string] }. Call AzureProvider.complete("last", prompt). Parse the JSON response into a Dag struct. Apply skills: for each skill name in skills, call SkillEngine.inject_into_nodes(skill_name, dag).

fn run_deep_research(question: String, depth: String, session_id: String) – Initialize a todo list [question]. Initialize an empty draft report string. Loop until todo list is empty or 50 iterations reached: (1) Pop the first todo item. (2) Call ExaClient.search(item, num_results: 100, summary: true). (3) Publish source_found events to WebSocket for each result. (4) Call the orchestrator model with the question, current draft, and Exa results, asking it to: (a) extend the draft with new findings, (b) list new questions to add to the todo list. (5) Parse the model response to extract new questions and the updated draft. (6) Add new questions to the todo list. (7) Update the draft in SingleStore. (8) Publish draft_updated event with the full draft. After loop, publish research_complete event.

 backend/src/orchestrator/dag_executor.inko

Implement Kahn's algorithm for topological sort. Maintain three collections: pending: Map[String, DagNode], running: Map[String, Channel[SubAgentResult]], completed: Map[String, SubAgentResult]. Main loop: compute all nodes whose depends_on are fully in completed. For each such node, remove from pending, spawn a new Inko process running SubAgent.run(node, build_context(completed)), store the result channel in running. Wait for any channel in running to receive a result. When a result arrives: move the node to completed, run ResultVerifier.verify(result, node), if verdict is Incomplete or Ungrounded, reenqueue the node with a retry counter (max 2 retries). Update SingleStore and publish WebSocket event after each node transition. After all nodes complete, return DagResult.

Spending cap enforcement: after each node completes, sum all tokens_used in completed. If the sum exceeds spending_cap, drain pending and mark all remaining nodes as skipped. Publish a cap_reached WebSocket event.

 backend/src/orchestrator/sub_agent.inko

Implement SubAgent with method fn run(node: DagNode, context: HandoffPayload) -> SubAgentResult. The run loop:

1. Build the full prompt: system prefix from context.style_spec, then context.parent_summary, then context.prior_findings formatted as numbered evidence list, then the task description.
2. Call the provider selected by node.model_preference via MetaRouter.select.
3. Parse the model response for tool call requests. The model must output tool calls in JSON blocks: {"tool": "tool_name", "params": {...}}.
4. For each tool call: check node.tools_allowed — if the tool is not in the allowed list, respond to the model with an error. Check reversibility: if node.reversibility == "irreversible", generate a UUID action ID, write the action details to Dragonfly key pending_approval:{action_id}, publish a approval_required WebSocket event, then poll Dragonfly key approval:{action_id} every 2 seconds for up to 120 seconds. If rejected or timeout, return SubAgentResult with status: "rejected". If approved, execute the tool.
5. Feed the tool observation back into the conversation as a new user message.
6. Repeat from step 2 with the full conversation history.
7. Detect diminishing returns: compute Jaccard similarity between the last three model outputs. If all three similarities exceed 0.95, terminate the loop.
8. Return SubAgentResult { output, citations, tool_calls_made, tokens_used, status, model_used }.

The summary is capped at 300 tokens by calling the Zig runtime /compact endpoint. The style spec is read from the workflow's associated skill, or defaults to: tone=neutral, format=markdown, paragraph_max_sentences=5, list_style=none.

 LAYER 3 – ZIG RUNTIME (port 9001, utility services)

 runtime/src/main.zig

Implement a minimal HTTP/1.1 server on port 9001 using std.net. Accept connections, read the request line and headers, dispatch to handlers by path:

 POST /count → token_counter.count_tokens(body)
 POST /compact → context_compactor.compact(body_json)
 POST /schedule → parallel_scheduler.schedule(body_json)
 POST /latency → latency_tracker.record(body_json)
 GET /latency_stats → latency_tracker.stats()

Write JSON responses with Content-Type: application/json and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

 runtime/src/token_counter.zig

Embed the cl100k_base BPE vocabulary using @embedFile("cl100k_base.tiktoken"). Implement the BPE tokenization algorithm: (1) byteencode the input string, (2) apply regex pretokenization splitting on whitespace, punctuation, and Unicode categories, (3) merge byte pairs iteratively according to the vocabulary merge table. Expose fn countTokens(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, text: []const u8) usize and fn truncateToTokens(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, text: []const u8, max_tokens: usize) []const u8.

 runtime/src/context_compactor.zig

Accept JSON body { "messages": [...], "target_tokens": int }. Algorithm: always keep the first message (system prompt) and the last 4 messages intact. For all middle messages, extract sentences containing: capitalized proper nouns, numeric values, modal verbs (must, should, will), or decision markers (decided, confirmed, rejected). Format the extracted sentences as a compact bullet list. Count tokens of the final assembly using token_counter.countTokens. If still over budget, truncate the bullet list from the end. Return { "messages": [...] } with the compacted assembly. The returned structure has three elements: system message, one summary message containing the bullet list, and the last 4 original messages.

 runtime/src/parallel_scheduler.zig

Accept JSON body { "tasks": [{ "id": string, "estimated_ms": int, "depends_on": [string] }] }. Implement list scheduling: (1) topological sort using Kahn's algorithm, (2) assign each task to the earliest available parallel slot considering dependencies, (3) return { "schedule": [{ "task_id": string, "slot": int, "start_ms": int, "end_ms": int }], "critical_path_ms": int, "total_slots": int }.

 runtime/src/latency_tracker.zig

Implement a ring buffer of size 1000 per provider. Accept POST body { "provider": string, "latency_ms": int }. Compute p50, p95, p99 via partial sort. Return { "providers": { "azure": { "p50": int, "p95": int, "p99": int }, ... } } on GET.
